audit_page_description: A health check for everyone's Continue Watching list. It flags items that shouldn't be there — already-finished shows, barely-started ones, or stale leftovers — so you can tidy them up. An empty result is normal and means nothing is wrong.
audit_help_what: Continue Watching is built from each user's playback progress. Occasionally an item gets stuck on that list — for example a show that was actually finished, or an old episode that a newer one has replaced. This page checks every user's list and shows only the items that look wrong.
audit_help_when: You normally won't need this page. Reach for it if users report odd entries in Continue Watching, or after importing history from another server (e.g. a Jellyfin sync) that may have marked many items at once.
audit_help_safe: Browsing here changes nothing. The only action that alters data is removing a suspected bulk-mark batch, which asks for confirmation first and is described before you confirm.
audit_inv_already_finished_help: This item is marked as watched but is still showing in Continue Watching. (invariant: is-not-watched)
audit_inv_watched_to_end_help: Progress is past the finish line, so it should have cleared itself off the list automatically. (invariant: not-complete-by-ratio)
audit_inv_barely_started_help: Less than 10% watched — probably too little to belong in Continue Watching. (invariant: has-min-progress)
audit_inv_music_item_help: Music doesn't belong in Continue Watching. (invariant: not-music-type)
audit_inv_abandoned_help: Not touched in over 60 days — most likely abandoned and safe to drop from the list. (invariant: not-stale-beyond-60d)
audit_inv_stale_duplicate_help: A newer "Next Up" episode already supersedes this lingering one, so it's a stale duplicate of the same series. (phantom shadow)

setup_warn_transport_mixed: Your proxy reports HTTPS, but its address is not in TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS, so {appName} ignores its forwarded headers. Add the proxy's IP to TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS, or set ORIGIN to your HTTPS URL.
setup_warn_transport_plaintext: {appName} is served over plain HTTP, so built-in login sends passwords unencrypted. Put it behind HTTPS before anyone outside your local network can reach it.
setup_warn_proxy_failclosed: TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS is not set. After setup, identity headers from a peer that is not trusted are rejected. Set TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS to your proxy's IP addresses (or LUMASTRA_TRUST_ANY_PROXY=true on a single host) so sign-in keeps working.
setup_warn_proxy_trustany: LUMASTRA_TRUST_ANY_PROXY=true trusts identity headers from any peer. That is only safe if nothing can reach {appName} directly. Setting TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS to your proxy's addresses is safer.
setup_warn_oidc_insecure: AUTH_OIDC_ALLOW_INSECURE=true turns off TLS verification for all OIDC traffic. Someone on the network could then forge an ID token and sign in as admin. Use it only with a local test provider, never in production.
setup_warn_oidc_scopes: AUTH_OIDC_SCOPES is missing "openid", so your provider won't return an ID token and sign-in will fail. Set AUTH_OIDC_SCOPES="openid profile email".
setup_warn_oidc_client: AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET is empty. Set it to the secret from your provider's application registration (leave empty only for a public client using PKCE).
setup_warn_oidc_link_username: AUTH_OIDC_LINK_BY_USERNAME=true lets a sign-in take over an existing account with the same username. That is only safe if your provider controls who gets which username. Linking by verified email is safer.
setup_oidc_test_ok: Discovery worked. Your provider is reachable.
setup_oidc_test_scopes_missing: Your provider doesn't advertise the requested scope(s): {scopes}. Sign-in may still work, but double-check your provider configuration.
setup_oidc_test_pkce_warn: Your provider doesn't advertise PKCE (S256) support. {appName} uses PKCE, so sign-in may fail unless your provider supports it.
setup_oidc_test_insecure: TLS verification was off for this test (AUTH_OIDC_ALLOW_INSECURE). Never use that in production.
setup_oidc_test_groups_info: The first sign-in must be in an admin group ({groups}), read from the "{claim}" claim. Make sure your provider releases that claim in the ID token.
setup_oidc_test_groups_missing: Your provider's discovery doesn't advertise a "{claim}" claim. If it doesn't release group memberships (you may need a groups scope or a claim mapper), the first admin sign-in will be rejected.
setup_oidc_test_email_missing: Your provider doesn't advertise an "email" claim. Linking OIDC sign-ins to existing accounts by verified email won't work without it.

setup_locked_intro: First-run setup was completed on this server, but no administrator can be found any more. Setup does not reopen by itself: that would let anyone who can reach this page create a new administrator.
setup_locked_cause: This usually means the identity provider no longer sends the admin group (it was renamed, or the last administrator was removed from it), or ADMIN_GROUPS no longer matches it.
setup_locked_idp_text: Add your account back to a group listed in ADMIN_GROUPS at your identity provider, or correct ADMIN_GROUPS. You are an administrator again on your next request (forward auth) or your next sign-in (single sign-on).
setup_locked_unlock_text: If you run the server, set SETUP_UNLOCK=1 in the container environment and recreate the container, or run this command inside the running container:
setup_locked_unlock_after: Until an administrator exists, anyone who can reach /setup can use it, and can even take over an existing username. Unlock only briefly, keep the server off the network meanwhile (or limit it to your own address), open /setup and create the administrator right away, then remove SETUP_UNLOCK. Setup locks again as soon as the administrator exists. Unlocking does nothing while any administrator exists.

setup_s3_backup_key_unknown: Also preserve the encryption key: back up the .env file or LUMASTRA_MASTER_KEY value if supplied through the environment, otherwise the master.key file in your config directory. Without the key, stored secrets cannot be recovered.
setup_s3_backup_env_key: Separately back up your .env file (or the LUMASTRA_MASTER_KEY value supplied through the environment). This environment-provided key is not automatically saved in the config directory; without it, stored secrets cannot be recovered.

setup_pref_lyrics_desc: From LRCLIB, when a lyrics tab is opened.

setup_pref_metadata_desc: Otherwise stored centrally under /config. Falls back to central if a folder isn't writable.

setup_pref_license_contact_desc: iPhone and Apple TV push notifications go through the standard relay, which needs a token from lumastra.org. Only the install ID and the Lumastra version are sent, nothing about your media or users. On a new install nothing has been sent yet: the first call waits for this answer. Off: this server never contacts lumastra.org.
setup_license_contact_off_warning: Without contact, push notifications on iPhone and Apple TV do not work through the standard relay. Nothing else changes. You can turn it on later in Admin → Settings → General → Push relay.
setup_pref_unrated: Show unrated content to age-restricted users
setup_pref_unrated_desc: Off by default, so items without a rating stay hidden from these users.
setup_pref_share_activity_desc: Choose who may see shared activity. Each person controls their sharing under Settings → Privacy; set the starting default below. Turning this off also hides live streams. Turning it back on does not restore them; use Playback settings.
setup_pref_show_unavailable: Show unavailable titles on discovery surfaces
setup_pref_show_unavailable_desc: Show catalog titles without local files on Trending and For You, so users can find and request them. Needs a request integration (Seerr or an external request URL); without one these titles stay hidden. Off: only media you can play is shown.
setup_pref_bcl_cascade_desc: When a user logs out at your identity provider (back-channel logout), also revoke their TV/mobile app sessions, not just the browser. Off = device apps keep their own sessions.

setup_metadata_lang_hint: The language for titles, descriptions and artwork from TMDB. Each library can use its own language later.
setup_metadata_additional_hint: Optional, up to 3, for households with several languages. Each user picks their display language in their own settings. You can add languages later; the missing metadata is then fetched automatically.
setup_metadata_additional_error_max: Max 3 languages after removing duplicates and your primary language.
setup_mdblist_hint: Optional. Adds ratings and curated lists, which also improve recommendations. You can add it later in Admin → Settings → Metadata.
setup_key_replace_hint: Leave blank to keep the current value, or enter a new one to replace it.
setup_discogs_hint: Optional. Adds Discogs as a source for artist metadata (discogs.com/settings/developers). It is only used while Discogs is in the enrichment chain, which you can change later in the settings of the “Fetch Artist Images & Bios” task.
setup_lastfm_hint: Optional. Used for artist popularity (free key at last.fm/api/account/create). You can add it later in the settings of the “Fetch Artist Popularity (Last.fm)” task.
setup_embed_recommend_hint: Optional. Embeddings are what the personal, similarity-based recommendations are built on.
setup_embed_dim_hint: The database stores {dim}-dimension embeddings (fixed when it was created), so your model must return {dim}-dimension vectors. OpenAI and Voyage do this on their own. setup_embed_dim_hint_unknown: Your embedding model must emit vectors matching the dimension the database was created with.

setup_embed_test_ok: Test string embedded: {dim}-dimension vector, matches the database.

setup_public_api_name: Allow apps and third-party clients (Public API)
setup_public_api_desc: Lets the Lumastra apps for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV sign in and receive push notifications. You sign in with your usual login, single sign-on included, by confirming a short code on this server. It also turns on the documented /api/v1 API for third-party players and scripts, separate from the Jellyfin-compatible /j API. Recommended. You can change it later under Admin → Settings → Access → Public API & Device Auth.
setup_public_api_off_warning: With this off, the Lumastra iPhone, iPad and Apple TV apps cannot sign in to this server, and /api/v1 is unavailable.
setup_jfcompat_desc: Lets Jellyfin apps and clients like Streamyfin connect to this server. Each person connects an app under Settings → Connections (app password or Quick Connect code), not with their web login. Turn off to make the /j API return 404.
setup_subsonic_desc: Lets Subsonic and OpenSubsonic apps such as Symfonium, Ultrasonic and DSub connect to your music library. Off by default. If your reverse proxy puts the whole app behind a login, /subsonic needs a bypass location too (see the install docs).

setup_lib_lede_more: Add another folder, or continue if you're done for now. You can always add more later in Settings.
setup_lib_path_hint: The absolute path where this media lives (inside the container, if you run in Docker).
setup_lib_type_hint: Pick what is in the folder. The scan looks for that type only, so the wrong type finds nothing.
setup_lib_audiobooks_hint: Audiobooks are not added as a folder. They come from Audiobookshelf, see above.
setup_abs_desc: Lumastra reads audiobooks from an Audiobookshelf server. Connect it here and pick which of its libraries to add.
setup_abs_url_hint: The address Lumastra uses to reach the server, for example the container name in Docker.
setup_abs_key_hint: Create it in Audiobookshelf under Settings > API Keys, for an admin user.
setup_abs_connected: Connected. Pick the libraries to add.
setup_abs_admin_matched: Your Lumastra account {username} can sync listening progress with Audiobookshelf ({matched}).
setup_abs_users_unmatched: Listening sync needs attention for: {names}. Ambiguous names or rejected personal keys cannot sync reliably; affected pulls are skipped. admin_pbquality_tooltip_health_score:
Health Score (0-100) measures playback quality.
• 90-100: Excellent - smooth playback
• 70-89: Good - minor issues
• 50-69: Fair - noticeable buffering
• 0-49: Poor - frequent interruptions

Factors: bandwidth ratio, rebuffering, server response time, buffer health
admin_pbquality_tooltip_bandwidth:
Average measured download bandwidth across all sessions.

Bandwidth Ratio = bandwidth ÷ video bitrate
• > 1.2x: Healthy headroom
• 1.0-1.2x: Tight, may buffer on spikes
• < 1.0x: Insufficient, will rebuffer
admin_pbquality_tooltip_rebuffers:
Count of rebuffering events where playback stalled waiting for data.

Common causes:
• Insufficient bandwidth for video bitrate
• Network instability/packet loss
• Server-side bottlenecks
• Transcoding too slow
admin_pbquality_tooltip_server_errors:
HTTP errors from the streaming server (4xx/5xx responses).

May indicate:
• File access issues
• Transcoding failures
• Server overload
• Network timeouts
admin_pbquality_tooltip_compression:
Compression ratio for transcoded streams.

ratio = source bitrate ÷ output bitrate

Higher ratio = more compression
• 2.0x: Output is half the source bitrate
• 1.0x: No bitrate reduction

admin_pbquality_tooltip_delivery:
How long the server took to send each video segment, across all sessions in this range.
• p50: a typical segment
• p95 / p99: the slow tail

A rising tail points at the server or its storage, not at the viewer's connection.

admin_glossary_task_definition: A background job's definition — what it does and how it's configured. Running it produces one or more Runs.
admin_glossary_run_definition: One execution of a task, start to finish — with its own status, timing, and log.
admin_glossary_step_definition: One stage in the pipeline a run passes through on its way to completion (e.g. probing a file, fetching metadata, generating previews).
admin_glossary_circuit_breaker_definitio: Lumastra pauses a task by itself after it fails repeatedly, so it stops retrying in a tight loop. It tries again on its own later; Resume now starts it immediately once you have fixed the cause.
admin_glossary_dead_letter_definition: Items that no longer retry automatically. Some failures cannot be retried; others reached the retry limit. Review the recorded reason before retrying or changing the source.
admin_glossary_needs_reidentification_de: Items that failed permanently because the data is wrong — e.g. the wrong media type, or an external ID (TMDB/IMDb) that no longer resolves. Retrying cannot fix these; re-identify the item, or accept it as expected if it genuinely is not on the provider.
admin_glossary_stuck_wedged_definition: A pipeline step that has stopped making progress — too many attempts, waiting too long, or nothing finished by its handler recently.
admin_glossary_resource_class_definition: A pool a task runs in (cpu, io, embedding…) with its own concurrency limit, so heavy tasks don't starve light ones.
admin_glossary_leader_election_definitio: In a multi-replica deployment, one node is elected leader per resource class to process its queue — the others stand by.
admin_glossary_degraded_component_defini: A core subsystem (database, cache, task orchestrator, …) is reporting unhealthy. Critical components can stall the whole app; others just reduce a feature until they recover. Open System Health for the failing check and its reason.
admin_glossary_setup_incomplete_definiti: A first-run setup step is still pending (e.g. adding a library folder or connecting metadata). This is informational, not an error — finishing setup unlocks the related features.
admin_glossary_failed_run_spike_definiti: A task has failed several times in the last 24 hours but its circuit breaker has not tripped yet — an early warning. Investigate the cause; pause or stop the task if it is hammering a failing dependency.
admin_glossary_overdue_schedule_definiti: A scheduled task has not run when expected (beyond a grace period). Run it now, or check why the scheduler stopped starting it.
admin_glossary_optional_integration_defi: An optional add-on data source (Last.fm, Discogs, MDBList). Lumastra works fully without it; adding a key just enriches metadata. This is informational, not an error — acknowledge it to dismiss until you decide to configure the integration.
admin_glossary_stage_definition: One step in the processing pipeline an item passes through (e.g. probing a file, fetching metadata, generating embeddings); each item moves stage by stage until fully processed.
admin_glossary_reconciler_definition: A background sweep that reclaims items left in a bad state — for example tasks orphaned by a crashed worker or stages stuck mid-run — so they can be picked up and retried.
admin_glossary_stage_sweep_definition: A periodic pass that finds items ready to advance and enqueues their next pipeline stage, keeping work flowing through the pipeline.
admin_glossary_event_dispatcher_definiti: Drains queued internal events (the event outbox) and delivers them to their handlers; events it can never deliver are set aside as dead-letters.
admin_glossary_scheduler_definition: Fires recurring jobs on a timer (like cron) — for example nightly syncs or periodic health checks — by enqueueing them when they are due.
admin_glossary_pending_write_drain_defin: Flushes buffered database writes that were queued up rather than written immediately; its depth is how many writes are still waiting to be persisted.
admin_glossary_backlog_definition: Work that has piled up waiting to be processed; a growing backlog means items are arriving faster than they can be handled.

admin_help_tasks_intro: This page explains the Task Catalog, Runs and Pipeline pages.
admin_help_catalog_p1: The task list shows every background job Lumastra runs, grouped by what it is for: library processing, music & AI, live TV, watch sync and maintenance. Tasks stay in name order and never move around.
admin_help_catalog_p2: Each row shows when the task last ran and how long it took, when it runs next, and a progress bar while it runs. A task with a problem keeps its place but turns amber with a one-line reason, and is also listed under “Needs attention” at the top, with the action that fixes it. A task that failed enough times in a row pauses itself (its circuit breaker) — more on that below.
admin_help_catalog_p3: Most tasks run themselves on a schedule; a few only run on demand. Run starts a task right now instead of waiting; clicking its name opens its details, run history and settings.
admin_help_catalog_p4: Tasks that delete or rewrite data always ask for confirmation before running.
admin_help_runs_p1: A run is one execution of a task — for example, one pass of enriching metadata or scanning a library.
admin_help_runs_p2: Use the Running, Failed, and Completed filters, plus a time window, to narrow down what you're looking at.
admin_help_runs_p3: Opening a run shows a summary, its individual steps, and the full log.
admin_help_runs_p4: When the same failure repeats back-to-back, those runs are grouped into a single streak.
admin_help_runs_p5: Amber failures are usually self-healing — things like rate limits or quota limits that resolve on their own. Red failures are the ones that need a look.
admin_help_pipeline_p1: The pipeline is drawn as a metro map: each line is a media type — movies, series & episodes, or music — and each station along the line is one processing step.
admin_help_pipeline_p2: A train stops at the leftmost station whose step is not done yet. That is the step currently pending for the item.
admin_help_pipeline_p3: A train parked in red means that step failed for that item. Once every step that applies to an item is finished, its train reaches the end of the line.
admin_help_pipeline_p4: The Completion view shows the same information as a per-item grid instead of a map — handy for scanning many items at once.
admin_help_pipeline_p5: Below the map, the Stuck items, Stopped retrying and Error groups panels list items that need attention.
admin_help_circuit_breaker_p1: When a task fails several times in a row, Lumastra pauses it automatically so it stops retrying in a tight loop.
admin_help_circuit_breaker_p2: While paused, it periodically lets one run through on its own to check whether the underlying problem has cleared up. That's the half-open state.
admin_help_circuit_breaker_p3: Resume forces that check to happen right now instead of waiting. Fix whatever caused the failures first — if the cause is still there, the task will just pause itself again.
admin_help_backlog_vs_runs_p1: These three numbers are often confused. Here is what each one means.
admin_help_backlog_vs_runs_p2: Backlog is how many items are waiting to be processed by a task.
admin_help_backlog_vs_runs_p3: Runs are executions of the task itself — a single run can process many items.
admin_help_backlog_vs_runs_p4: Failures happen at two levels: a whole run can fail, or specific items (particular movies or episodes) can fail one step while the run around them otherwise succeeds. Those per-item failures show up as Stopped retrying on the Pipeline page.
admin_help_when_red_intro: A short checklist for triaging a problem, top to bottom:
admin_help_when_red_step1: Check whether the task has a paused banner.
admin_help_when_red_step2: Open the task and read its plain-language failure line.
admin_help_when_red_step3: Most transient problems heal on their own at the next scheduled run.
admin_help_when_red_step4: If a task paused itself, fix the underlying cause first, then use Resume.
admin_help_when_red_step5: For problems tied to specific items, check the Pipeline page — each row links straight to that item's Fix page.
admin_circuit_learn_more_body: Lumastra pauses a task automatically after it fails several times in a row, so it stops retrying in a tight loop. While paused, it occasionally allows one run to check whether the problem is resolved. Resume now runs that check immediately.
admin_tasks_help_healthy: A green check means the last run succeeded and there is nothing for you to do. Problems are listed under “Needs attention” at the top, each with the action that fixes it.
admin_tasks_help_paused: A task that failed enough times pauses itself. Open it, fix whatever is causing the failures, then use Resume to let it try again.

admin_attention_integrity_detail_season_: Some seasons aren't correctly linked to their series — the same kind of structural problem, one level up. Re-scanning the library usually repairs the link.

admin_quarantine_empty_body: Hidden and automatically cleared warnings are in Warning history. Episode move proposals are listed separately below.
admin_quarantine_dismiss_confirm_body: Marks every unresolved row for this series as dismissed. This cannot be undone.
admin_quarantine_dismiss_success: Hidden warnings: {count}. Show again is available in Warning history.
admin_quarantine_dismiss_failed: Warnings could not be hidden. Refresh and try again.
admin_quarantine_accept_none: No decisions were resolved in this batch. Unresolved decisions remain for review.
admin_quarantine_help_reason_proposed: an episode without an identity lines up by episode number with an episode of the TMDB catalog in another season (typically a series whose releases are numbered across seasons). Nothing was changed. Dismiss the row to stop proposing the pair; to apply such matches on their own, turn on "Auto-apply episode matches based on numbers alone" in the settings.
admin_quarantine_moves_help: Episodes the automatic reconciliation bound to a TMDB episode, some of them moved into another season. Undo puts an episode back where it was, restores its title and removes the TMDB id it was given. The next metadata sync recreates the episode it was merged with, and the same match is not applied again.
admin_quarantine_moves_undo_confirm_body: The episode returns to season {season}, episode {episode} and loses the TMDB id it was given. The next metadata sync recreates the episode it was merged with. Watch state, ratings and playlist entries that were merged from that episode stay on this episode. The same match will not be applied again.
admin_quarantine_proposals_help: Matches the automatic reconciliation did not apply on its own, because only the episode numbers (or a file name without a usable title) back them. Apply gives the episode the TMDB identity and moves it to that position; it shows up under applied moves, where you can undo it. Dismiss keeps the episode where it is and blocks the match for good.
admin_quarantine_proposals_evidence_unti: Number in the file name, no title to compare
admin_quarantine_proposals_evidence_file: Number in the file name, title matches (automatic apply is off)
admin_quarantine_proposals_apply_confirm: The episode moves from S{fromSeason}E{fromEpisode} to S{toSeason}E{toEpisode} and takes the TMDB episode {title} as its identity. The placeholder episode at that position is merged into it. You can undo the move afterwards.
admin_quarantine_proposals_dismiss_confi: The episode stays where it is and this match is not proposed again.
admin_quarantine_help_what: The reconciliation backfill re-checks each episode's stored identity against TMDB by matching its chapter titles (or, if it has none, its filename) to the official episode list. Confident changes are applied automatically. Uncertain changes are held here instead, where you can review them in bulk, grouped by series.
admin_quarantine_help_why: An episode lands in quarantine when the matcher's result is a near-miss rather than a clean hit. The Reasons column tags each row with why:
admin_quarantine_help_reason_matched: a specific episode proposal was recorded. Review batch shows only unchanged decisions with complete eligible dependencies. Already-applied identity-bound decisions can be checked with Recheck.
admin_quarantine_help_reason_below: no single sufficiently supported candidate was recorded. The warning remains open for manual investigation; Accept cannot repair it.
admin_quarantine_help_reason_duplicate: multiple episodes claimed the same identity. Investigate the source data; Accept cannot invent an unambiguous decision.
admin_quarantine_help_rows: The count covers all current warnings in the group, including later inspection pages. Recheck and Apply examine bounded batches; Continue reaches later warnings. Hide covers the exact group shown and can be reversed from Warning history. Proposed moves keep their own manual actions.
admin_quarantine_help_accept: Reviews up to 1,000 applicable decisions in complete dependency components before confirmation. Retained seed warnings are also counted and shown. Continue to reach later warnings. Changed or oversized components require individual review.
admin_quarantine_help_dismiss: hides the current warning revisions for this series without changing episodes. Warning history can show the original batch again. Changed warnings require a fresh list.

admin_task_desc_file_library_scan: Scans your library folders on a schedule to catch files added while the server was offline or on network shares where instant change detection doesn't work.
admin_task_desc_file_delta_ingest: Adds or removes a specific list of files from the catalog without re-scanning the whole library.
admin_task_desc_file_reconcile: Runs a lightweight, frequent check for new or removed files on network-mounted libraries between full scans.
admin_task_desc_media_probe: Reads technical details — resolution, codecs, audio and subtitle tracks — from each media file.
admin_task_desc_tmdb_metadata_sync: Imports popular, trending, and top-rated movies and TV shows from TMDB into the discovery catalog.
admin_task_desc_metadata_sync: Fills in missing title and language details for movies and TV shows from TMDB.
admin_task_desc_metadata_update: Refreshes existing catalog items with IMDB IDs, cast, crew, and keywords from your configured metadata providers.
admin_task_desc_metadata_cast_backfill: Adds character names and photos to the cast of older library items that were synced before this data was captured.
admin_task_desc_metadata_aggregation_bac: Rebuilds an item's combined metadata summary from data already fetched, without calling external providers again.
admin_task_desc_metadata_translations_sy: Fetches title, overview, and episode text translations for your configured additional languages.
admin_task_desc_metadata_translations_se: Queues existing library items for a translation refresh, including ones that previously skipped it while translations were disabled.
admin_task_desc_mdblist_sync: Enriches discovery items with ratings, keywords, and streaming-availability info from MDBList.
admin_task_desc_curated_lists_sync: Refreshes curated content lists — trending, popular, and similar — from external sources.
admin_task_desc_fribb_anime_sync: Downloads a community-maintained mapping to add MyAnimeList and AniList IDs to your anime library.
admin_task_desc_mal_anime_id_enrichment: Maps individual anime episodes to their correct MyAnimeList list entries, so multi-part seasons sync correctly.
admin_task_desc_release_calendar_sync: Pulls upcoming and recently-aired episodes and movies from your Sonarr and Radarr calendars to keep the release calendar current.
admin_task_desc_airing_series_refresh: Re-syncs series that are still airing from TMDB, so newly announced episodes and seasons get their rows before the first file arrives.
admin_task_desc_image_sync: Re-scans a media item's folder for artwork files and matches them to the correct episode, season, or movie.
admin_task_desc_series_sync: Fully refreshes a TV series' metadata from TMDB, including all seasons and episodes.
admin_task_desc_bulk_media_sync: Re-syncs metadata from the provider for a batch of items selected in the media browser, one item at a time.
admin_task_desc_chapter_sync: Fetches chapter markers for a series from its metadata provider.
admin_task_desc_trickplay_generation: Generates the scrubbing preview thumbnails shown when seeking through a video.
admin_task_desc_auto_identify_personal_m: Finds online matches for unresolved items. Entries are never combined or removed by this task.
admin_task_desc_episode_thumbnail_backfi: Generates missing episode thumbnail images, extracting a frame from the video when no artwork file exists.
admin_task_desc_integrity_scanner: Regularly checks the catalog for structural problems so they can be reviewed before they cause playback issues.
admin_task_desc_lumastra_intro_analyzer: Detects intro, outro, recap, and preview segments in episodes so the player can offer skip buttons.
admin_task_desc_lumastra_intro_analyzer_: Resumes intro and credits detection where the last run stopped when it reached its time limit.
admin_task_desc_album_enrichment: Fetches cover art and MusicBrainz release IDs for albums missing artwork, from your configured music metadata sources.
admin_task_desc_artist_enrichment: Fetches images and biography details for music artists from your configured music metadata sources.
admin_task_desc_discovery_embeddings: Generates AI recommendation embeddings for catalog items you don't own yet, powering discovery recommendations.
admin_task_desc_library_embeddings: Generates AI recommendation embeddings for the movies and shows in your library.
admin_task_desc_lyrics_ingestion_backfil: Indexes track lyrics for full-text lyrics search, from on-disk lyric files or previously-fetched lyrics.
admin_task_desc_lyrics_lrclib_fetch: Downloads lyrics from LRCLIB for tracks that don't have any yet.
admin_task_desc_mood_vector_generation: Builds the mood profile data (e.g. energetic, calm) used by mood-based music recommendations.
admin_task_desc_music_embedding_generati: Generates AI recommendation embeddings for music tracks.
admin_task_desc_acoustid_fingerprint: Identifies tracks that have no MusicBrainz tags by their sound, using your AcoustID key.
admin_task_desc_music_popularity: Fetches listener counts and play-count popularity data for artists from Last.fm.
admin_task_desc_profile_backfill: Builds AI taste profiles for users with enough watch history but no profile yet, powering personalized recommendations.
admin_task_desc_sonic_clustering: Groups tracks with similar sound into clusters, powering sound-based music discovery.
admin_task_desc_music_genre_centroids: Builds an audio fingerprint for each music genre so the app can suggest a genre you have never played but are likely to enjoy.
admin_task_desc_sonic_embedding_backfill: Analyzes track audio to generate sound-based embeddings for similarity search and recommendations.
admin_task_desc_sonic_map_projection: Projects the sound-based track embeddings onto a 2D map for the music discovery map view.
admin_task_desc_music_embedding_projecti: One-time setup: fits the compact sound-similarity model the offline download pool uses to pick the next track, from your library's existing audio embeddings.
Applies the fitted sound-similarity model to tracks that don't have a compact version yet, so the offline download pool can rank them.
admin_task_desc_music_analysis: Analyzes track audio for tempo, key, energy, and mood so tracks can be searched and mixed by sound.
admin_task_desc_import_m3u: Imports channels from an M3U playlist source into your Live TV lineup.
admin_task_desc_import_epg: Imports the program guide schedule data from an EPG source.
admin_task_desc_refresh_m3u: Re-fetches an M3U source's channel list on its configured schedule to pick up changes.
admin_task_desc_refresh_epg: Re-fetches an EPG source's program guide on its configured schedule to keep the schedule current.
admin_task_desc_watch_sync_manual: Runs a one-off manual Import or Export against a single watch-sync provider for one user, on demand rather than on the 5-minute schedule.
admin_task_desc_watch_sync_pull: Imports watch progress and history from all enabled watch-sync providers every 5 minutes.
admin_task_desc_watch_sync_push: Sends your locally-changed watch progress to all enabled watch-sync providers every 5 minutes.
admin_task_desc_jellyfin_watch_sync_push: Registry entry for the Jellyfin watch-sync provider's push side — the sync engine drives it directly, it can't be run on its own.
admin_task_desc_jellyfin_file_inventory: Matches Jellyfin items to your files by path when they have no shared TMDB or IMDb id, so their watch progress can sync.
admin_task_desc_jellyfin_watch_sync_pull: Registry entry for the Jellyfin watch-sync provider's pull side — the sync engine drives it directly, it can't be run on its own.

Registry entry for the AudiobookShelf watch-sync provider's pull side — the sync engine drives it directly, it can't be run on its own.

admin_task_desc_library_storage_snapshot: Records the size of each library and the free space of the disks they are on, once a day, for the growth chart and the disk-full estimate on the admin home.
admin_task_desc_health_invariants: Runs a set of database health checks every 15 minutes and records any drift so problems surface before they become critical.
admin_task_desc_oauth_cleanup: Removes expired login tokens, sessions, and orphaned device links.
admin_task_desc_play_session_cleanup: Marks playback sessions that stopped sending heartbeats as crashed, finalizing ones that had actually finished.
admin_task_desc_task_history_retention: Moves old task run history into an archive table so admin dashboards and queries stay fast as history grows.
admin_task_desc_telemetry_cleanup: Removes old playback-quality telemetry data past its retention window.
admin_task_desc_plugin_update_check: Re-reads your plugin repositories and flags which installed plugins have a newer version on offer. It never installs anything — you still choose.
admin_task_desc_music_transcode_cache_re: Keeps the music transcode cache under its configured size limit by removing the least-recently-used files.
admin_task_desc_valkey_memory_monitor: Watches Valkey's memory usage and logs warnings as it approaches its memory limit, before the task queue could get stuck.
admin_task_desc_watch_history_retention: Removes watch-history entries older than the configured retention window.

admin_task_desc_never_owned_media_gc: Deletes movies and series that were never in your library and that nothing references once they pass the configured age; while the cleanup is off in Settings it only reports what it would delete.
admin_task_desc_artwork_reaper: Removes artwork records whose image file no longer exists on disk, so an item falls back to its inherited artwork instead of showing nothing. Skips checks entirely while a library share looks offline.
admin_task_desc_stage_sweep: Works through the backlog of pending pipeline steps — metadata, images, embeddings, and more — across the whole library, keeping every stage moving.
admin_task_desc_embedding_reset: One-shot: deletes existing AI embeddings for a chosen source and re-queues them for regeneration, e.g. after a model change.
admin_task_desc_episode_thumbnail_genera: Generates a thumbnail for episodes that have no artwork file at all, by sampling several frames from the video and keeping the best one. Skips the intro and end credits, and rejects black or blank frames.
admin_task_desc_reconciliation_backfill: Re-checks existing series against newly-available data to fix historical episode mis-matches, flagging uncertain cases for review instead of guessing.

admin_fix_proxy_intro: Shows which identity headers your reverse proxy sent with this page request, which takes the same path as a login. Only whether each header arrived is shown, not its value.
admin_fix_proxy_verdict_ok: Your proxy is sending identity correctly, and this server trusts it.
admin_fix_proxy_verdict_no_headers: No identity headers arrived. The proxy is not sending them, or is sending them under different names than this server expects.
admin_fix_proxy_verdict_untrusted: Identity headers arrived but were DISCARDED, because the machine that connected is not in the trusted list. Logins will fail without an error message.
admin_fix_proxy_verdict_failclosed: No trusted-proxy list is configured and implicit trust is off, so identity headers are rejected from everyone. Nobody can sign in.
admin_fix_proxy_verdict_disabled: Forward auth is turned off (FORWARD_AUTH_ENABLED), so identity headers are ignored from every machine, trusted or not. Turn it on only if you sign in through a forward-auth proxy, and only after your proxy removes any identity headers a client sends itself and TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS lists only the proxy. It is set in the server environment, not in Admin settings.
admin_fix_proxy_verdict_user_unusable: The username header ({header}) arrived, but it is empty or contains curly braces, which means the proxy sent its header template instead of the value. This server ignores it, so nobody can sign in. Fix the header mapping in your proxy.
admin_fix_proxy_trust_warning_address_he: ADDRESS_HEADER is set, so the connecting address above is read from a request header a client can choose, not from the connection. Anyone can then pretend to be your proxy and sign in as any user. Unset ADDRESS_HEADER while forward auth is on.
admin_fix_proxy_trust_warning_trust_any: Identity headers are accepted from every machine that can connect (LUMASTRA_TRUST_ANY_PROXY). Anyone who can reach this server without going through the proxy can sign in as any user, including an admin. Set TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS to the proxy's address instead.
admin_fix_proxy_trust_warning_wide_range: TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS contains a range wider than /24. Every machine in that range can send identity headers itself and sign in as any user, including an admin. List only the address of each proxy.
admin_fix_proxy_peer_note: This is the address your trusted-proxy list must contain. It is the address the proxy connects FROM, which is often not the address users type.
admin_fix_proxy_posture_allowlist: A trusted-proxy list is configured and enforced.
admin_fix_proxy_posture_trustany: No list configured; identity headers are accepted from any connecting machine.
admin_fix_proxy_posture_failclosed: No list configured and no opt-in — identity headers are rejected from everyone.
admin_fix_proxy_privacy_note: Header values are hidden because they identify users and may come from an untrusted source.
admin_fix_proxy_purpose_user: Who the proxy says you are. Without it nobody can sign in.
admin_fix_proxy_purpose_groups: Your groups, which decide admin rights and library access.
admin_fix_proxy_purpose_client_ip: The original client address. Used for rate limits and audit entries.
admin_fix_proxy_purpose_proto: Whether the user reached the proxy over HTTPS. If this is wrong, links and redirects can be built with the wrong scheme.
admin_fix_proxy_purpose_host: The Host header this app received.

Duration differences alone do not prove damage. admin_attention_recovery_orphans_detail: A job stopped mid-run and the system cleaned it up and queued it again. Restarts and updates are already excluded from this count, so these happened while the server was running normally. The usual causes are a worker being killed for using too much memory, a container restarting on its own, or jobs running longer than their time limit. Check the worker container's memory limit and restart count first.
admin_attention_recovery_boot_detail: Each restart runs a recovery pass over jobs that were in flight. Planned updates are already excluded, so these look like unplanned restarts — typically an out-of-memory kill or a crash loop. Check the container exit codes and memory limit.
admin_attention_recovery_events_detail: Events that keep the library in sync (new files, metadata changes) failed to process and were queued again. Nothing is lost, but repeated retries usually mean the database or cache is under strain, or one event is failing over and over.
admin_attention_recovery_stagesweep_deta: More library work is waiting than the server will queue at once, so it is being fed through in batches. This is normal right after adding a lot of media and should settle on its own; if it persists for days, the workers are not keeping up with the library size.
admin_attention_cluster_mismatch_detail: Key fingerprints in use (node count): {groups}. Set LUMASTRA_MASTER_KEY to the same value on every replica, or mount the config directory as a shared volume. Until then, logins and encrypted credentials only work on whichever replica holds the matching key.

admin_fix_sp_poster_lede: Posters come from the metadata provider an item is matched to. A missing poster usually means the match is missing or failed, not that the image is broken.
admin_fix_sp_poster_body: If the poster is missing, look for the item under Fix matches; items listed there have no provider to fetch artwork from. If the poster shows the wrong film, the item is matched incorrectly (see the separate entry on this page). If the item is matched correctly and still has no poster, the provider has none; retries are recorded in the poster backfill task.
admin_fix_sp_subtitles_lede: Missing subtitles and out-of-sync subtitles have different causes and fixes. Check which one applies first.
admin_fix_sp_subtitles_body: Subtitles are either embedded in the video file and detected when the file is probed, or stored as separate files next to it and detected during a scan. Subtitle files added after the last scan are not detected yet. Out-of-sync subtitles are almost always timed for a different release of the same title.
admin_fix_sp_music_art_lede: Album art and artist images come from different sources. Album art usually comes from the tags in your audio files; artist images are fetched from a provider.
admin_fix_sp_music_art_body: Missing artist images mean the lookup has not run yet or found nothing. Wrong album art usually means the file tags differ from what you expect. Lumastra displays artists exactly as tagged and does not rewrite them. Correct the tags and rescan to update the display.
admin_fix_sp_stale_clients_lede: When a phone or TV app shows outdated information, it is usually showing its own cached copy.
admin_fix_sp_stale_clients_body: Open the same item in the admin media browser. If the server shows the new information, the app's cache is outdated; close and reopen the app, or sign out and back in. If the server also shows the old information, the problem is on the server side, for example the metadata or the files.

admin_fix_match_lede: A wrong match means the file is linked to the wrong entry at the metadata provider. Change the match on each affected item.
admin_fix_match_warning_title: Do not refresh metadata on everything
admin_fix_match_warning_body: A full metadata refresh queues every item in the library, which can take hours and use a lot of CPU. It also does not fix a wrong match, because the same wrong entry is fetched again. Change the match instead.
admin_fix_match_cta_broken: Fix matches — items whose match broke
admin_fix_match_cta_never: Fix matches — items that never matched

admin_fix_files_description: Checked on this server as this page loaded: whether scanning is on, whether each library folder is there and readable, and what the last scan found.
admin_fix_files_scan_disabled: Scanning is turned off on this server. No new files are detected, by scheduled or manual scans, until it is turned back on.
admin_fix_files_scan_disabled_how: This is the DISABLE_FILE_LIBRARY_SCAN setting, typically set during storage maintenance.
admin_fix_files_scan_paused: The library scan is paused, so it will not fire on its own.
admin_fix_files_scan_never: This server has not scheduled a library scan yet. On a fresh install that resolves itself once the background worker has started for the first time.
admin_fix_files_scan_unreadable: The scan schedule could not be read, so this page cannot say whether scanning is on. Check again in a moment.
admin_fix_files_paths_none: No library folders are configured yet, which is why nothing is showing up. Add one under Sources & scanning.
admin_fix_files_state_denied: There, but this server cannot read it
admin_fix_files_state_remote: Remote library — nothing on this disk to check
admin_fix_files_timeout_body: The folder is configured, but the filesystem did not respond within four seconds. This usually means a network share whose server is unreachable. A hung mount is not reported as missing.
admin_fix_files_denied_lede: This server runs as uid {uid}, but the folder is owned by uid {owner} with permissions {mode}. With these permissions the server cannot read it.
admin_fix_files_denied_lede_noowner: This server runs as uid {uid} and cannot read the folder's details. The permission problem is on this folder or one of its parent folders.
admin_fix_files_denied_pick_one: Apply one of the following fixes.
admin_fix_files_fix_chown_label: Give the folder to this server
admin_fix_files_fix_chown_hint: Changes who owns the files. Do not run it on a share that another program also writes to.
admin_fix_files_fix_chmod_label: Or make it readable by everyone
admin_fix_files_fix_chmod_hint: Leaves ownership alone. The capital X sets the traverse bit on folders only, so your video files are not marked executable.
admin_fix_files_fix_compose_label: Or run this server as the folder's owner
admin_fix_files_fix_compose_hint: Add this to your docker-compose.yml and recreate the container. Nothing on disk changes.
admin_fix_files_fix_inspect_label: To see what is there right now
admin_fix_files_missing_safe_count: The {count} items in this library are still listed and have not been removed.
admin_fix_files_missing_safe_why: When a library folder is missing or unreadable, the scanner sees an incomplete listing and refuses to remove anything from your catalogue. Reconnect the folder and everything comes back on the next scan.
admin_fix_files_missing_empty: This library has no items, so there is nothing to compare against. Reconnect the folder and check again.
admin_fix_files_missing_count_unknown: The items in this library could not be counted, so this page cannot confirm that nothing was removed. Reconnect the folder and check again.
admin_fix_files_missing_next: Common causes: a network share that did not remount after a reboot, a renamed Docker volume, or a drive that is not mounted.
admin_fix_files_hold_heading: Removed files are not being cleaned up
admin_fix_files_hold_few: The last scan found {walked} of the {known} files the library knows in this folder, so it removed nothing: that is what an offline or half-mounted share looks like. Every scan since {since} has done the same.
admin_fix_files_hold_none: The last scan found no files in this folder, although the library knows {known}, so it removed nothing: that is what an offline or unmounted share looks like. Every scan since {since} has done the same.
admin_fix_files_hold_check: Check that the share is mounted and complete. If the files really were deleted, remove them from the library: the next scan of this folder does it once.
admin_fix_files_hold_confirm: Remove the {missing} missing files from the library? Titles left without a file are hidden; their watch history is kept.
admin_fix_files_hold_confirmed: Confirmed. The next scan of this folder removes the missing files.
admin_fix_files_last_scan_none: This folder has never been scanned.
admin_fix_files_last_scan_unreadable: The last scan of this folder could not be read.
admin_fix_files_last_scan_running: A scan is running here right now.
admin_fix_files_last_scan_abandoned: The last scan here did not finish — the server restarted or the run was lost while it was working.
admin_fix_files_last_scan_unmatched: {count} could not be matched to anything.
admin_fix_files_last_scan_zero_added: It added nothing new. If you were expecting a new file, the scan either ran before you added it, or it saw the file and could not match it.
admin_fix_files_pipeline_heading: Where new files are in processing
admin_fix_files_pipeline_body: {inFlight} items are partway through processing, {running} are being worked on right now.
admin_fix_files_pipeline_oldest: The longest-waiting item has been waiting {age}.
admin_fix_files_pipeline_failed: {failed} failed in the last hour and {dead} have given up entirely.
admin_fix_files_pipeline_idle: Nothing is waiting in processing — anything the scan found has already been dealt with.
admin_fix_files_process_line: This server is running as uid {uid}, gid {gid}.
admin_fix_files_process_unknown: This platform does not report a user id for the server process, so the ownership advice below does not apply.
admin_attention_disk_low_detail: {free} free of {total} ({percent}% used). Transcoding, image caching and new downloads all write here — when it reaches zero those start failing rather than slowing down.
admin_attention_disk_full_detail: Only {free} left of {total}. Writes to this volume are failing or about to fail. Free space here before anything else.
admin_fix_slow_description: Current server load, measured when this page loaded: background work, playback, memory and disk.
admin_fix_slow_unreadable: Some parts of this page could not be read and are left out: {sections}.
admin_fix_slow_worker_none: No background worker is available, so nothing is being processed. Pausing lanes will not help.
admin_fix_slow_worker_unknown: Whether a background worker is running could not be checked, because the cluster state did not answer.
admin_fix_slow_expected_yes: This is expected. Your library is still being processed for the first time: {remaining} items are queued and {done} finished in the last five minutes. Background CPU usage drops once first-run processing is complete.
admin_fix_slow_expected_incremental: Your library has already been processed. {remaining} new or changed items are queued and {done} finished in the last five minutes. That is routine catch-up work and should not keep the CPU busy for long. If the load stays high, check the lanes and playback below.
admin_fix_slow_expected_stalled: {remaining} items are queued for processing, but nothing finished in the last five minutes. Processing appears to be stuck.
admin_fix_slow_expected_done: First-run processing has finished — every stage has worked through its queue, so background CPU use should already be near zero. Sustained load now points at playback rather than at background work.
admin_fix_slow_lane_idle: Nothing is queued or running in any lane.
admin_fix_slow_pause_hint: Pausing prevents new jobs from starting in that lane. Running jobs finish normally and are not cancelled.
admin_fix_slow_fewer_body: The number of jobs a lane can run at once is a setting and takes effect after a restart. Pausing takes effect immediately; lowering the limit is permanent.
admin_fix_slow_playback_none: No transcodes are running, so playback is not what is loading this server.
admin_fix_slow_playback_unknown: Running transcodes could not be counted, so this page cannot say whether playback is loading the server.
admin_fix_slow_playback_jobs: {jobs} transcode(s) running, using about {cpu}% CPU between them.
admin_fix_slow_playback_hint: Transcoding uses more CPU than anything else. A single 4K transcode can fully load a small server.
admin_fix_slow_memory_limited: This server may use {limit} of memory, and is currently using {used}.
admin_fix_slow_memory_limit_only: This server is capped at {limit} of memory.
admin_fix_slow_memory_uncapped: No container memory limit is set, so this server may use the host's {host}.
admin_fix_slow_memory_unknown: The container memory limit could not be read, so it is unknown whether this server is limited below the host's {host}.
admin_fix_slow_memory_note: Memory figures elsewhere in the admin area show the host's memory. This value shows the container's memory limit, which is what applies to this server.
admin_fix_slow_cpu_budget: This container may use {effective} of the host's {host} CPU cores.
admin_fix_slow_disk_unmeasured: {volume} could not be measured ({reason}). A mount that does not answer is a common cause of a slow server.
admin_fix_slow_disk_paths_failed: The library folders could not be read, so only the config and transcode volumes were measured.
admin_fix_slow_disk_hint: When a volume is full, transcodes, image caching and scans fail.
admin_fix_slow_paused_toast: {lane} lane paused. It stays paused, also across restarts, until you resume it.

admin_task_impact_problem_derive: The notification bell stops updating, so new problems are not reported.
admin_tasks_tier_common_hint: The most commonly used tasks. The rest are internal maintenance tasks that run automatically.
admin_tasks_tier_common_empty: None of the common tasks are registered on this server.

admin_setup_reassure_watch: You can start watching now. The remaining details are added in the background.
admin_setup_reassure_cpu: High CPU usage is normal for the next few hours.
admin_setup_not_started_note: These are not counted in the progress above, because nothing has run yet to measure. If one is still at zero once setup finishes, it is switched off or missing an API key.
admin_setup_problems_pending: Problems are being collected and will be shown together when setup finishes.

admin_run_error_provider_auth: A metadata provider rejected the API key.
admin_run_error_provider_auth_hint: Nothing will succeed on retry until the key is fixed — re-enter it in the metadata provider settings.
admin_run_error_rate_limited: The provider asked us to slow down.
admin_run_error_rate_limited_hint: Expected during a large first scan. Lumastra slows down its requests and continues automatically.
admin_run_error_media_decode: The media file could not be decoded — it looks damaged.
admin_run_error_media_decode_hint: Playback of this file may also stutter or fail. Replace the file, or skip it from now on.
admin_run_error_ffmpeg_missing: ffmpeg is not where Lumastra expects it.
admin_run_error_ffmpeg_missing_hint: Thumbnails, scrubbing previews and transcoding stay unavailable until the ffmpeg path is set in the settings.
admin_run_error_disk_full_hint: Everything that writes files is paused to protect the database; your library and playback are unaffected. Free up space, then start the run again.
admin_run_error_permission_denied: Lumastra is not allowed to read that folder.
admin_run_error_permission_denied_hint: Nothing there is read until the folder's owner and permissions let Lumastra's user in.
admin_run_error_path_missing: A folder or file Lumastra expected has disappeared.
admin_run_error_path_missing_hint: Usually a drive that did not mount, or a changed Docker volume. Nothing has been deleted — items already in your library are safe. Check again once the path is back.
admin_run_error_no_network: Lumastra cannot reach the internet — a name lookup failed.
admin_run_error_no_network_hint: Everything that needs the internet is paused and resumes by itself. Your library and local playback are unaffected.
admin_run_error_no_match: The provider had no match for this title.
admin_run_error_no_match_hint: Usually a naming problem rather than a fault — match the item by hand, or rename the file to follow the naming guide.
admin_run_error_db_constraint: Something went wrong inside Lumastra while saving.
admin_run_error_db_constraint_hint: This is a bug on our side, not a problem with your setup — the affected item was skipped and nothing was damaged. Please report it with the technical details below.
admin_run_error_task_paused: Paused after several failures in a row.
admin_run_error_task_paused_hint: Lumastra stopped retrying so it does not hammer a service that is down, and tries once by itself later. Fix the cause of the last failure first — resuming without that just pauses it again.
admin_run_error_subtitle_timeout: Extracting subtitles took too long for this file.
admin_run_error_subtitle_timeout_hint: Image-based subtitles on a long film can exceed the time limit. Playback still works — those subtitles are rendered live instead, using a little more CPU. Raise the limit, or skip this file.
admin_run_error_worker_oom: A background job was killed — the server most likely ran out of memory.
admin_run_error_worker_oom_hint: Lower how many jobs run at once, or give the container more memory, then start the run again.
admin_run_error_plugin_crash: A plugin crashed and was turned off for now.
admin_run_error_plugin_crash_hint: Your other providers keep working. Look for a plugin update, then switch it back on.
admin_home_load_controls_pause_desc: Temporarily stops all background tasks, freeing disk and network for whatever else needs them.
admin_home_load_controls_work_profile_er: Couldn't save the work profile — try again.
admin_task_desc_pause_reconcile: Checks every minute whether a global pause or quiet-hours window has expired and resumes the paused queues.
admin_task_impact_pause_reconcile: A 'pause everything' or quiet-hours window may not end on schedule, leaving background processing stopped.

admin_circuit_explain_monitoring: Lumastra is watching this task. If it fails several times in a row, it is paused automatically so it stops retrying in a tight loop.

admin_sessions_terminate_local_note: This only clears the entry here — the file is on the device and keeps playing.

admin_redesign_tasks_ondemand_hint: Tasks with no schedule — they run when a scan, a button, or another task asks for them.
admin_task_from_plugin_title: Added by the installed plugin “{id}”, not part of Lumastra itself.
admin_attention_section_stale_hint: None of these has changed in over a week. Acknowledge the ones you expect, so a new problem stands out here.
admin_ops_hero_not_applicable: {count} items skip some steps — they have no video track, or the step does not apply to them
admin_attention_plugin_failures_detail_n: The rest of your library is unaffected. Open the task to see which items failed and why. This task cannot retry single items: fix the cause, then run the task again.
admin_failure_patterns_none_task: No new failures in the last {window}. Items that failed earlier and are still unresolved are listed below.

config_apns_key_p8_description: Contents of the APNs authentication key Apple issued you, starting with "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----". Set this only if you build and distribute your own iOS app. Paste the file contents here, or use the path setting below instead; setting both is an error. Saving validates the PEM, P-256 curve, key ID and team ID locally and applies changes immediately, with no restart. Apple’s acceptance can only be confirmed by a real delivery. The APNs topic is the bundle identifier registered by each device.
config_feature_music_clustering_descript: When enabled, the Quick Picks "taste-similar" bucket uses k-means clustering over your top-played track embeddings to surface tracks from each distinct mode of your listening (e.g. workout vs. chill). Disable to fall back to the legacy single-centroid recommendation that averages all your tastes into one. Cached 6h per user. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_alchemy_description: Enable the Music Alchemy mixing desk (/music/alchemy) and brew API, which lets users drop seed tracks, twist Energy/Tempo/Obscurity knobs, and brew a ranked playlist from the acoustic library. Default off; requires analysed tracks (bpm/energy/mood_tags) and Music Quick Picks Multi-Mode Taste Clustering. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_sonic_description: Enable the MSCLAP audio-level embedding pipeline for sound-based track similarity ("sounds like this"). Default off; requires a GPU worker running the sonic-embedder container and AI Recommendations enabled. Run the "Sonic Embeddings Backfill" task after enabling. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_map_description: Enable the 2D UMAP projection starfield at /music/map. Visualises all tracks in the library as coloured dots based on their MSCLAP audio embeddings. Requires FEATURE_MUSIC_SONIC and umap-learn installed in the sonic-embedder container. Run the "Sonic Map Projection" task from /admin/tasks after enabling. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_lyrics_search_descr: Enable semantic lyrics search at /music/lyrics-search. Embeds .lrc sidecar files using the voyage embedding provider and allows kNN "search by lyric phrase" queries. Requires AI Recommendations. Run the "Lyrics Ingestion Backfill" task after enabling. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_clusters_descriptio: Enable KMeans clustering of the MSCLAP 1024-dim audio-embedding space into auto-generated playlists at /music/collections. Run the "Sonic Clustering" task from /admin/tasks to populate assignments in media_audio_clusters. Each cluster gets a derived label from dominant essentia mood_tags (or "Sonic Mix N"). Requires Sonic Embeddings (FEATURE_MUSIC_SONIC). Default OFF. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_text_sound_descript: Enable natural-language track search at /music/text-search using the MSCLAP joint text+audio embedding space. Queries like "calm piano" or "aggressive metal" are encoded into a 1024-dim CLAP text vector and matched via kNN over media_audio_embeddings. Requires Sonic Embeddings (FEATURE_MUSIC_SONIC). Default OFF. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_sonic_taste_descrip: Enable on-demand Rocchio personalisation in the MSCLAP 1024-dim vector space. Builds a per-user sonic taste vector from up/down votes (user_ratings) and play/skip counts (user_music_state), then replaces the metadata-based "taste-similar" Quick Picks bucket with a "sonic-taste" kNN bucket over media_audio_embeddings. Falls back to metadata taste automatically when the user has no signal yet (cold-start). Requires Sonic Embeddings (FEATURE_MUSIC_SONIC). Default OFF. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_sonic_queue_descrip: Make the autoplay / next-track queue a sonic blend: similarity to the current queue and mood + your personal sonic taste profile (up-votes), while excluding down-voted and skipped tracks. Falls back to the existing queue picker when off or on cold-start (no taste / empty queue). Requires Sonic Embeddings (FEATURE_MUSIC_SONIC). Default OFF. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_first_description: When enabled, visiting '/' redirects to '/music' and the sidebar reorders to put music navigation at the top. Independent of Music Alchemy. No restart needed.
config_instance_primary_mode_description: Content-mode axis for this instance. 'vod' (default) = film/TV-first layout; 'music' = music-first layout; 'mixed' = balanced layout. Orthogonal to the capability flags (FEATURE_MUSIC_ALCHEMY, FEATURE_MUSIC_FIRST). No restart needed.
config_music_autoplay_top_k_description: How many top scored candidates the autoplay next-track is sampled from (weighted by similarity). 1 = deterministic, always the best match, may feel repetitive. 5 = balanced variety (recommended). No restart needed.
config_music_autoplay_seed_anchor_weight: How strongly autoplay pulls each hop back toward the first track of the session. Without an anchor the queue drifts toward your dominant taste cluster after a few hops. 0 = disabled, expect drift. 0.15 = gentle anchor (recommended). 0.3 = strong anchor, may feel stuck in long sessions. No restart needed.
config_music_autoplay_min_track_seconds_: Excludes very short tracks (album intros, interludes, skits) from autoplay, queue suggestions, and Quick Picks. 0 = disabled. 90 = recommended (catches intros and short transition tracks). Tracks with missing duration metadata are kept regardless. No restart needed.
config_music_autoplay_max_track_seconds_: Excludes very long tracks (full compilations, DJ sets, audiobook-like files) from autoplay, queue suggestions, and Quick Picks. 0 = disabled. 900 = 15 minutes (recommended). Tracks with missing duration metadata are kept regardless. No restart needed.
config_music_popularity_weight_descripti: How strongly provider popularity (e.g. Last.fm listener counts) biases the smart queue. 0 = off. 0.3 = gentle nudge toward well-known tracks. 1 = full influence, obscure remixes heavily demoted. Requires the Music Popularity sync plugin and an API key. No restart needed.
config_music_popularity_exponent_descrip: Power curve applied to popularity scores before multiplying into the smart queue. 1 = linear (big demotion for obscure tracks). 0.5 = sqrt (gentler demotion, recommended). 0.33 = cube-root (very mild). Lower values flatten the curve so even deep cuts compete. No restart needed.
config_music_popularity_floor_descriptio: Minimum popularity factor so no track is hard-excluded; guarantees deep cuts still appear occasionally. 0.1 = zero-scored tracks stay eligible at 10% weight (recommended). 0 = strict exclusion of zero-score tracks. No restart needed.
config_music_popularity_primary_source_d: Which popularity provider the smart queue reads from. Additional providers (ListenBrainz, local playcounts) may ship in future releases. Must match an installed Music Popularity provider. No restart needed.
config_music_sonic_queue_min_candidates_: Minimum number of MSCLAP audio candidates the sonic queue must find before use; below this it falls back to the metadata embedding path, which has better diversity with small pools. 0 = legacy behavior. 5 = recommended. No restart needed.
config_music_autoplay_genre_streak_weigh: How strongly a same-genre listening streak biases autoplay: matching candidates are boosted and zero-overlap candidates are penalized by up to this amount; untagged candidates are unaffected. 0 = disabled (legacy). 0.25 = recommended. No restart needed.
config_music_autoplay_genre_streak_cohes: How dominant one genre must be across your recent listening history before autoplay treats it as an active streak and applies the genre-affinity boost/penalty. Lower triggers more readily; higher needs a near-uniform recent history. 0.5 = recommended. No restart needed.
config_feature_music_transcode_descripti: Enable on-the-fly music transcoding. When enabled, clients can request tracks in a different format or bitrate (e.g. MP3 192 kbps from a FLAC source). Disable to serve only the original file. No restart needed.
admin_connection_key_required: Enter the API key to test a different server.
admin_connection_url_invalid: Enter an http:// or https:// URL.
setup_tmdb_invalid_key: TMDB rejected the API key (HTTP 401). Check the key and try again.
setup_tmdb_verification_warning: The TMDB key was saved, but could not be verified: {reason} Metadata requests will retry automatically.
setup_jellyfin_invalid_token: The API key contains characters that are not allowed. Copy it again from Jellyfin (Dashboard > API Keys).
setup_jellyfin_url_credentials: Remove the user name and password from the address; Jellyfin connects with the API key only.
setup_jellyfin_unreachable: Could not reach Jellyfin at {address} ({cause}). Check the address and that Jellyfin is running.
admin_provider_calls_note: Web and worker HTTP attempts, including retries. Current hour is partial. Errors include all 4xx, 5xx and network failures; 429s are also errors. Counters start when enabled and may lose a small number of calls during outages or restarts.
admin_library_detail_age_limit_hint: Users below this age don't see this library. Audiobooks in it count as at least this age. Movies and series keep their own age rating.
admin_users_age_unrated_count_hidden: {unrated} of {total} library titles have no age rating, so age-limited users cannot see them. The Age Rating Backfill task fills them in from the national rating.
admin_users_age_unrated_count_visible: {unrated} of {total} library titles have no age rating. Age-limited users can see them because unrated content is allowed.
admin_task_desc_age_rating_backfill: Looks up the national age rating (FSK, MPAA, BBFC and so on) of titles that have none or only an MDBList rating, and replaces the MDBList age with it. Runs in small batches, so it can take a while on a large library.
admin_task_impact_age_rating_backfill: Age-limited users may not see titles that have no age rating, or see them under an age that does not match the national rating.
admin_library_path_remote_fixed: The upstream library cannot be changed. Remove this library and add the other one instead.
admin_library_path_create_library_first: Create a library first, then add folders to it.
admin_library_path_fallback_hint: Tried in order when the primary provider finds no match. Useful for anime libraries: set primary to TMDB, add AniDB as fallback.
admin_library_path_edition_hint: Auto-tags files from this path with the given edition when the filename has no explicit edition.
admin_library_path_server_path_hint: Only needed when the media server’s path differs from the container path. Leave blank if they match.
admin_library_path_not_found: Folder “{folder}” was not found. Check the path and that it is mounted into the container.
admin_library_path_is_file: “{folder}” is a file, not a folder.
admin_library_path_unreadable: Folder “{folder}” is not readable by Lumastra. Check the container user’s permissions.
admin_library_path_empty: Folder “{folder}” is empty. It will find no media until you add files.
admin_library_path_remote_added: Added {name}. The first sync will start shortly.
admin_library_remote_activity_hint: Catalog imports use {source}; see sync runs for the latest activity.
setup_jf_sync_interval: Watch history syncs in the background every 5 minutes by default; changes may take until the next sync to appear.
admin_library_remote_load_failed: The library list could not be loaded.
admin_library_remote_missing_keys: Set {keys} before you can pick a library.
admin_library_remote_list_failed: Could not read the {source} library list
admin_library_remote_empty: {source} is connected but reports no libraries. Create one there first.
admin_library_remote_all_added: Every {source} library is already added or cannot be ingested.
admin_library_remote_enable_existing: One or more are disabled. Re-enable them in the library list instead of adding them again.
